label: letter right after an "o g" bigram early in the original sequence (e.g. "x o g [m]")
explanation: Very sparse (0.01% of steps, never more than once per sequence), weak (max 0.20). The clearest and strongest part: original-phase steps 2-3 whose input is a letter like m/z/j/f/e/x/c/q coming right after the bigram "o g" ("l o g [m]", "x o g [m]", "o g [z]"). Within that part the top activations go with in_tok m. This clause has about 0.68 precision on dev but covers only about a third of the activation mass. The rest is scattered: other original-phase contexts with g or o two steps back ("l g g [j]", "l g o [m]", "o o [f]"), and about 27% of the mass in the copy phase, mostly at the last step of short sequences (L=3-4) when the fed-back input is z/m/x/s ("y r z k <DEL> y r [z]", "r m o <DEL> r [m]"). Copy-phase clauses had low precision. Never fires at t=0-1 or once the model has made a copy error, and almost never on the <DEL> step.
